why: Pins BMR-Review's ruling of 2026-10-19 (option a: keep the cap; corroboration cannot say WHICH part an un-numbered title is, 'you can't be sure which part', 2026-09-01). Moved from golden_pairs_pending with no version of its own: the behaviour is compare-spec 2.21.0's. A part number on ONE side only of an Episode pair ('The Long Night Part 2' against 'The Long Night'), bases agreeing, everything else identical, and TWO distinct identity Alt ID sources (IMDb + a proprietary domain) agreeing with no conflict. For an Episode/Season pair that is AMBIGUOUS, not a conflict (operator ruling 2026-10-19, "That's ambiguous"; compare-spec 2.21.0, eidr-core 0.69.0): cmp_titles reports part_ambiguous and not part_conflict, and BMR-Review's scorer caps it at REVIEW_TOP. Until 2.21.0 the comparator reported part_conflict for numbered-vs-bare, so with >= ALT_CORROBORATION_STRONG_MIN agreeing sources the scorer's part-number OVERRIDE branch fired, applied no cap, and the pair reached Accept. `verdict_not_in` Accept pins the cap. Mutation-tested: restoring the episode-unaware parts_conflict in cmp_titles makes this pair Accept and fails it, and no other pair; eidr-core 0.68.1 (spec 2.20.0) fails it the same way. The single-source sibling `episode-part-number-one-sided` passes under both rules (one source never reached the override), which is why this pair exists. SCOPE: the cap only -- not the comparator's 0.70 title score, and not the films' numbered-vs-bare conflict, which 2.21.0 left unchanged.
